_comment: Facts about this adapter that its probe response cannot carry: display names, maturity, and the engine versions CI actually restores from. Everything the probe declares (adapter version, engine id, source kinds, pitr) is read from testdata/probe_response.golden instead — never duplicated here. The capabilities generator fails if the source names below do not match the probe exactly, and the integration suite restores from the images listed under verified — the baseline on every run, the rest in the scheduled version matrix and before a release tag — so neither can drift. There is no official SQLite image; the community image below is the pragmatic verification target (any image carrying a POSIX shell and the sqlite3 CLI works, the README explains). SQLite's upstream supports only its latest release, so the older lines listed are the ones distributions maintain — the baseline is the line Debian stable ships, per docs/engine-versions.md §6. See docs/capabilities.md and docs/engine-versions.md.
name: SQLite

sources.sqlite_db: One database file from `sqlite3 .backup` or `VACUUM INTO` (or a copy of a cleanly closed database)
sources.sqlite_db_dir: A directory of database files; the newest by file time is restored (the header records no wall clock)
sources.sqlite_dump_dir: A directory of dumps; the newest by file time is restored
